chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Al-Qassim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Hazim narrated to us from his book, saying: Ubays ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jabla, from Ibrahim ibn al-Mustanir, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the master of this matter has two occultations. The first one is long, until some of them say: He has died, and some say: He has been killed, and some say: He has gone. So not remaining upon his matter from his companions except a small group, no one is informed of his place, neither a guardian nor other than him, except the Master who manages his affairs.

key_terms.صاحب الأمر: The Master of the Matter (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of the Imam and how does the first one affect the companions?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiqadiq outlines the doctrine of the two occultations, specifically detailing the Great Occultation (al-Ghaybah al-Kubra) characterized by widespread doubt and the scarcity of true adherents. It highlights the transition from the Four Imams to a single chief deputy (al-Mawla al-Akbar), ensuring the continuity of divine guidance while the Imam's physical presence remains concealed from both rulers and the general public.
